question: Your extraction system uses a coordinator agent that assigns each section of a supplier contract to a subagent. The pricing subagent has extracted three of the five required fields, but then its query to the internal rate-card database times out. The coordinator must decide how to complete the JSON output that downstream systems consume. What should the pricing subagent return to the coordinator?

options.text: Return a short generic status saying the rate-card lookup is unavailable, so the coordinator knows the pricing section failed and can route the entire section to human review.
options.reason: A generic error status hides the failure type, the attempted query and the partial results, so the coordinator cannot choose an intelligent recovery.

options.text: Raise an error that stops the entire extraction workflow for this contract, so that no partial pricing data reaches the downstream systems.
options.reason: Terminating the whole workflow on a single failure is an anti-pattern; it discards the partial results and other sections instead of enabling recovery.

options.text: Return the three extracted fields with the two missing fields left empty and a success status, so the downstream systems receive valid JSON without delay.
options.reason: Returning empty results as success silently suppresses the error, which the guide names as an anti-pattern because the coordinator never learns of the failure.

options.text: Return the failure type as a timeout, the rate-card query it attempted, the three extracted fields, and possible alternatives such as retrying or using the contract appendix.
options.reason: Structured error context with failure type, attempted query, partial results and alternatives lets the coordinator make an informed recovery decision.
